paper_metadata.title: Quantum-inspired variational algorithms for partial differential equations: Application to financial derivative pricing

summary: This paper presents a variational quantum Monte Carlo / neural-network quantum state method for solving high-dimensional PDEs and applies it to the d-dimensional diffusion equation and Black-Scholes option pricing. Reported results include 1D–4D diffusion relative errors from 5.13e-3 to 1.47e-1, runtime tables showing the method becomes faster than forward Euler at n=16 qubits, and 1D Black-Scholes option-pricing errors such as 0.011781 (Ours) versus 0.002494 (Euler) at the base setting; however, no gate-based quantum hardware is used and no practical quantum advantage is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Variational quantum Monte Carlo / neural-network quantum state solver for the d-dimensional diffusion (heat) equation with Gaussian initial conditions, benchmarked against forward Euler across 1D–4D and varying qubit counts.

algorithm.variant: Autoregressive neural-network quantum state (NQS) variational Monte Carlo with McLachlan variational principle
algorithm.ansatz: Masked autoregressive neural network / MADE-style conditional probability factorization
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Pre-training for 50k iterations; evolution run for 20k iterations in reported experiments

hyperparameters.learning_rate_schedule: warm-start for first 1/10 of total training iterations, then decay by factor 10 at 3/7 and 5/7 of total training iterations

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Pre-trained to match the initial condition using stochastic gradient descent/Adam before time evolution

optimizer_settings.learning_rate_schedule: warm-start then step decay at 3/7 and 5/7 of total iterations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Spatial domain discretized on a regular grid with 2^n points mapped to n-qubit computational basis states; each basis state corresponds to a mesh point in the d-dimensional hypercube
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize the McLachlan variational residual ||Phi_{t+dt,t}(u_theta) - u_{theta+delta_theta}||^2, leading to M(θ) θ' = V(t,θ) for the PDE evolution
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Boundary conditions implemented via source functions on the mesh; Dirichlet and periodic boundary conditions considered

problem_instance.description: d-dimensional diffusion/heat equation with Gaussian initial condition on a discretized hypercube; compared against forward Euler time stepping

dataset_specification.description: Gaussian initial state defined via modified Bessel function; experiments reported for 1D, 2D, 3D, and 4D cases with n/d = 4 or 5 qubits per dimension

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Spatial discretization on a regular grid; initial condition pre-trained on mesh points; Monte Carlo sampling from |psi_beta(x)|^2
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Average relative error over 20k iterations; running time over 2k iterations; averaged across exactly 5 seeds

hardware.framework: BackPack / deep learning software stack (quantum hardware not used or not specified)

implementation_details.classical_solver: Forward Euler finite-difference baseline; SVD regularization used to stabilize linear solve for parameter updates
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Mesh discretization; pre-training on initial condition; Monte Carlo sampling buffer with unique samples and counts; per-sample gradients via BackPack; CPU parallel extraction of sparse operator rows
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Relative error computation against Euler baseline; option-pricing mapping not part of this experiment

speedup_claims.conditions: For the mesh-based VMC/NQS solver with batch size B; forward pass O(TBn^2), sampling O(TBn^3), versus forward Euler O(T×2^(2n)) as stated in the paper
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes overhead from sampling, backward pass, and sparse row extraction; the method is approximate and uses implicit access to state entries.

speedup_claims.conditions: Reported in the timing table for the diffusion problem
speedup_claims.caveats: This crossover is based on the reported timing table; Euler could not be run for higher dimensions due to memory constraints.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(TB poly(n)); forward pass O(TBn^2), sampling O(TBn^3)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(T×2^(2n)) for forward Euler as stated in the paper
complexity_analysis.crossover_n: Reported as n=16 qubits where the proposed method becomes faster than forward Euler in their timing table

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Reported crossover at n=16 qubits in timing table, but this is within a software benchmark and not a hardware demonstration
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require scalable fault-tolerant gate-based hardware plus efficient state preparation/sampling; the paper uses a classical neural-network simulation stack
limiting_factors: Forward Euler is more accurate in the reported 1D benchmarks
No gate-based quantum device is used
The method is algorithmic/quantum-inspired rather than a hardware quantum computation
Sampling and per-sample gradient overhead dominate runtime

notes: This paper is quantum-inspired and does not report execution on a gate-based quantum device; hardware is therefore not specified.
The reported 'quantum' resources are algorithmic/model resources for the NQS/VMC method, not a physical circuit implementation.
The paper reports only software-based VMC/NQS simulations and compares against classical Euler; it does not demonstrate a quantum hardware advantage.
Table 1 shows relative errors up to 1.47e-1 in 4D, while Table 2 shows the method can become faster than Euler at n=16 qubits in runtime, but this is not a practical quantum advantage claim.

experiments.description: Application of the same autoregressive NQS/VMC PDE solver to 1D European call option pricing under the Black-Scholes model, benchmarked against the analytic Black-Scholes formula and forward Euler.

algorithm.variant: Autoregressive neural-network quantum state variational Monte Carlo for Black-Scholes PDE
algorithm.ansatz: Masked autoregressive neural network / MADE-style NQS
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Same training/evolution protocol as the diffusion experiments; results reported at expiration time T

hyperparameters.learning_rate_schedule: warm-start for first 1/10 of total training iterations, then decay by factor 10 at 3/7 and 5/7 of total training iterations

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Pre-trained to the initial payoff/boundary condition on the spatial mesh before time evolution

optimizer_settings.learning_rate_schedule: warm-start then step decay at 3/7 and 5/7 of total iterations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Black-Scholes PDE transformed to a heat equation on a truncated hypercube and discretized on a mesh mapped to n-qubit basis states
problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate the option price function V(t,s) by variational time evolution under the PDE residual using McLachlan’s principle
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Boundary values set using time-discounted payoff functions on the faces of the truncated hypercube

problem_instance.description: 1D European call option pricing under Black-Scholes; compared against analytic Black-Scholes formula and forward Euler; ablation over volatility, strike, interest rate, and expiry time

dataset_specification.description: European call payoff max(s-K,0) with parameter sweeps over sigma, r, K, and T; 1D and 2D option-pricing tables reported

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Transform Black-Scholes PDE to heat equation via change of variables; truncate domain to [Ke^{-3σ_i√T}, Ke^{3σ_i√T}]^d; discretize on mesh
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Relative error at expiration time T against analytic ground truth; compared to forward Euler; averaged over reported runs (5 seeds for the underlying solver experiments)

hardware.framework: BackPack / deep learning software stack (quantum hardware not used or not specified)

implementation_details.classical_solver: Forward Euler finite-difference baseline; analytic Black-Scholes formula used in 1D for ground truth
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: PDE-to-heat-equation variable transform; domain truncation; mesh discretization; payoff-based boundary conditions
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Relative error at expiration time; convexity plots versus strike price; comparison to analytic formula and Euler

algorithm.ansatz: Masked autoregressive neural network / MADE-style NQS

The paper states that increasing batch size can reduce relative error from about 15% to around 3% for a fixed problem size.

experiments.description: 1D Black-Scholes European call option pricing ablation over volatility, strike price, interest rate, and expiry time, compared against the analytic Black-Scholes formula and forward Euler.

algorithm.variant: Autoregressive NQS variational Monte Carlo for Black-Scholes PDE
algorithm.ansatz: Masked autoregressive neural network / MADE-style NQS

key_results: Table 4 reports 1D call-option relative errors for 'Ours' ranging from 0.010436 to 0.086764 depending on parameters.
The corresponding Euler errors range from 0.000328 to 0.002538, so Euler is consistently more accurate in 1D.

experiments.description: 2D Black-Scholes option-pricing experiments for basket call, basket put, rainbow max call, and spread put options.

algorithm.variant: Autoregressive NQS variational Monte Carlo for Black-Scholes PDE
algorithm.ansatz: Masked autoregressive neural network / MADE-style NQS

key_results: Table 4 reports relative errors of 0.053477 (basket call), 0.043926 (basket put), 0.057949 (rainbow max call), and 0.031574 (spread put).
No analytic ground truth is available for these 2D cases; comparison is against Euler only.
